messages:
alex_support: FYI customer reported sustained throughput drop and increased 5xx on Dedicated pool dp-42 since ~03:10 UTC. Reports: ~40% drop in tokens/sec, tail latency spikes. Samples attached.
cheng_infra: Which model & pool? any recent deploys? :eyes:
alex_support: Model: redwood-std-13b-fp16, region: us-west-2, pool: dp-42. No config deploys in the last 2 hours. Customer says requests stall in queue then 502s.
olivia_sre: Throwing up the queue/batcher metrics now. Quick check: batcher.microbatch_size.avg = 1.1 reqs, batcher.tokens_per_batch.avg = 320 (was ~2200 baseline). scheduler.window_ms = 10ms. Looks like lots of tiny batches.
ben_runtime: Tiny batches => throughput loss. Could be max_batch_tokens cap or clients sending many short prompts. Any noisy tenant activity on dp-42?
maria_oncall: Checking tenant map: big-retailer (tenant_id t-9002) has a burst of short chat-style requests starting 03:07. They have a lot of concurrent sessions.
cheng_infra: Also see continuous-batcher backpressure logs: "microbatch_emit: window_full_after_prefill" repeated. Prefill stalls and then emits tiny postfill batches.
alex_support: Customer side shows 502 with body: "upstream buffer overflow" and request_id=rcpt-0a12. Logs from runtime attached: ```2026-03-17T03:14:22Z ERROR serve: handler: send upstream fail: write: broken pipe``` 
ben_runtime: Likely two interacting issues: (1) max_batch_tokens too low -> batcher emits often; (2) scheduler quantum/window too small -> prefill not accumulating. Combined with noisy tenant generating many small messages, we get thin batches and autoscaler sees low token rate per instance so doesn't scale.
olivia_sre: Confirming autoscaler metrics: cpu_utilization ~25%, queued_requests high but token_rate_per_gpu low -> scaling policy is token_rate-based so it didn't trigger. Autoscaler allowed_max_replicas = 4, current_replicas = 3.
cheng_infra: Propose repro run: simulate noisy tenant by firing 400 TPS of 1-10 token prompts to pool dp-42 and monitor batch_size. Repro steps:
  1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/dp-42/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' --parallel 400
  2) watch metrics: `batcher.tokens_per_batch.avg`, `scheduler.window_ms`, `prefill_wait_count`
  3) tail runtime logs: `kubectl -n runtime logs -l pool=dp-42 -f`
ben_runtime: Quick mitigation hotfix: increase `max_batch_tokens` from 512 -> 4096 for dp-42 and raise `scheduler.window_ms` from 10ms -> 30ms to give prefill a chance. Also add tenant shaping: limit per-tenant concurrency to avoid one tenant creating many microbatches.
alex_support: Can we patch without a full deploy? Maybe dynamic config toggle?
deploy-bot: Scheduled config update for pool dp-42 at 2172501800: set max_batch_tokens=4096, scheduler.window_ms=30. (owner: cheng_infra)
cheng_infra: Will roll the config to dp-42 now as a staged change to one node first, then full pool. Also enabling `prefill_affinity=true` for warm KV cache affinity.
maria_oncall: After first node change, metrics: tokens_per_batch.avg -> 1800, latency p95 improved from 420ms -> 210ms, 5xx down from 7.2% -> 1.1%. Customer reports partial recovery.
olivia_sre: Note: autoscaler scaling policy needs to consider request count spikes from small-token requests; will open a follow-up to add combined metric (token_rate + request_rate) to avoid under-scaling.
ben_runtime: Follow-up action items: 1) add tenant concurrency cap (short term) 2) update default `max_batch_tokens` for similar pools 3) add a canary test simulating noisy-tenant microburst 4) update runbook with playbook commands for quick toggle
alex_support: Customer notified that we applied a config change and are monitoring. They'll confirm in 30m. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
cheng_infra: I'll keep the staged rollout under 1 hour and post rollback if regressions. Tagging @maria_oncall for postmortem and billing impact check.
maria_oncall: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-274 with notes, marking for severity P2. Will track billing anomalies for affected customers.
ben_runtime: To avoid recurrence we should also add an alert on `batcher.tokens_per_batch.avg < 800 && queued_requests > 200` so ops get paged earlier.
alex_support: Awesome. Closing Slack thread once postmortem created. Good job team.
